title: Make the XOR of All Segments Equal to Zero
statement:
You get an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`. A segment `[left, right]` with `left <= right` has as its XOR the bitwise XOR of every element from index `left` through index `right`, both ends included.

In one change you may overwrite a single element of `nums` with any integer you like. Return the fewest elements you must change so that every segment of exactly `k` consecutive elements has XOR equal to `0`.
notes:
## Intuition

Two neighbouring windows `[i, i+k-1]` and `[i+1, i+k]` share `k-1` elements, so if both XOR to 0 then `nums[i] === nums[i+k]`. The final array must therefore repeat with period `k`, and its first `k` values must XOR to 0. Split the indices into `k` groups by `i % k`: each group ends up holding a single value, and the group values must XOR to 0. A group set to `v` costs its size minus how many of its elements already equal `v`.

Trying every combination of group values is exponential. Instead, process the groups one at a time like a knapsack, where the "capacity" is the XOR so far (only 1024 possibilities because values are below 2^10).

## Approach

1. `dp[x]` is the fewest changes for the groups handled so far whose chosen values XOR to `x`. Start with `dp[0] = 0`.
2. For each `group`, tally `count` of its values and its `size`.
3. Option A: overwrite the whole group with an arbitrary value. Then any target XOR is reachable from the cheapest state, so every `next[x]` starts at `best + size`.
4. Option B: keep a value `value` that already appears `freq` times. From state `x` this reaches `x ^ value` at cost `dp[x] + size - freq`.
5. After all groups, `dp[0]` is the answer.

Option B only needs values present in the group: any other value costs the full `size`, which option A already covers.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1,2,0,3,0]`, `k = 1`: one group holding all five values, `size = 5`, `count = {1:1, 2:1, 0:2, 3:1}`. Option A gives every `next[x] = 0 + 5`. Option B from `x = 0` gives `next[1] = 4`, `next[2] = 4`, `next[0] = 3`, `next[3] = 4`. The answer is `dp[0] = 3`: turn 1, 2 and 3 into 0.

## Complexity

- Time: O(1024 · n): each group scans 1024 states times its distinct values, and the distinct values over all groups total at most `n`.
- Space: O(1024 + n) for the two DP rows and the counts.

## Pitfalls

- Restricting option B to values in the group is safe only because option A covers "any other value" through `best`; forgetting option A gives wrong answers when every group must be rewritten.
- Groups have different sizes when `k` does not divide `n`; count `size` per group.
- Start `dp` with `Infinity` except `dp[0]`, so impossible XOR states are not used before the first group.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `MAX` | number of possible XOR values (2^10) |
| `dp` | fewest changes per XOR value for the groups done so far |
| `group` | current residue class `i % k` |
| `count`, `size` | value frequencies and length of the current group |
| `best` | smallest entry of `dp`, used when the group is fully rewritten |
| `next` | the DP row after adding this group |
| `x`, `value`, `freq`, `cost` | previous XOR, kept value, its frequency, and the resulting cost |

narration.2: Values are below 2^10, so any XOR of them is one of 1024 values.
narration.3: dp[x] holds the fewest changes so far for an XOR of x; unreachable states are Infinity.
narration.4: Before any group is chosen the XOR is 0 at no cost.
narration.5: Handle the k groups of indices that share the same remainder modulo k.
narration.8: Walk the indices of this group, k apart.
narration.9: Tally how often each value already appears in the group.
narration.12: The cheapest state so far, used when the whole group is overwritten.
narration.13: Rewriting every element of the group with a free value can reach any XOR at cost best + size.
narration.15: ...combined with keeping a value that already appears in this group.
narration.16: Keeping value costs one change for each element that is not already value.
narration.17: Keep the cheaper way of reaching XOR x ^ value.
narration.21: The new row replaces the old one before the next group.
narration.23: All groups are chosen; the answer is the cost of making their XOR 0.
